title: Probability: Dependent and Independent Events, Tree Diagrams and Contingency Tables
seo_title: Grade 11 Probability Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Dependent and independent events; the product rule for independent events: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B); Venn diagrams, tree diagrams and two-way contingency tables to solve probability problems (where events are not necessarily independent).
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 11 probability worksheets: dependent and independent events, the product rule, tree diagrams and contingency tables. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Independent: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Independent events: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).
  • Without replacement, the second probability changes: one fewer item.
  • In a tree diagram, multiply along the branches and add the end results you want.
  • In a contingency table, check independence: is P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B)?

Examples

Example

2 red and 3 blue; take two without replacement

P(red, red) = 2/5 × 1/4

Answer: 1/10

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
AddingAnd means multiply.
Without replacementReduce the total by 1.
The totalUse the grand total for P(A and B).

items.q: A and B are independent. P(A) = 0,1 and P(B) = 0,4. Find P(A and B).
items.e: For independent events, multiply: P(A and B) = 0,1 × 0,4 = 0,04.

items.q: P(A) = 0,7, P(B) = 0,6 and P(A and B) = 0,42. Are A and B independent?
c: Yes, because P(A) × P(B) = P(A and B)
No, because P(A) × P(B) ≠ P(A and B)
items.e: P(A) × P(B) = 0,7 × 0,6 = 0,42, which equals P(A and B) = 0,42. Yes, because P(A) × P(B) = P(A and B).

items.q: A pack has 10 cards, and 5 of them are picture cards. Two cards are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are picture cards.
items.e: 12 × 49 = 29. The second fraction has one fewer card of each.

items.q: The probability that Aisha passes Paper 1 is 710 and Paper 2 is 45, independently. Find the probability that she passes exactly one paper.
items.e: Pass 1 and fail 2, or fail 1 and pass 2: 710 × 15 + 310 × 45 = 1950.

items.q: A fair die is rolled 2 times. Find the probability of getting at least one six.
items.e: P(no six) = (56)2 = 2536. P(at least one six) = 1 − 2536 = 1136.

items.q: A fair die is rolled 3 times. Find the probability of getting at least one six.

items.q: A bag has 3 black marbles and 6 white marbles. Palesa takes two marbles without replacement. What is the probability both are black?
items.e: First black: 3/9. One black is gone, so the second is 2/8. 13 × 14 = 112.

subject: maths
